digest.component_or_area: LLM model class configuration and routing
propositions: Four hand-built LLM sub-calls (overlap-judge, ticket-digest, ticket-quality, code-novelty) bypass model-class configuration and inherit raw cfg.model, routing to direct Anthropic instead of configured Bedrock
overlap-judge dominates plan-review traffic at 18 of 23 calls, making it the highest-volume bypass site and most visible to operators attempting cutover via class configuration

ticket-digest runs on the store write path (enrich_drain.maybe_drain called from event_append and push), sending ticket content to direct Anthropic during routine comment/create operations outside any gate

With class vocabulary configured differently from cfg.model, no hand-built sub-call in review-plan, review-code, or verify-completion should resolve to cfg.model; currently all four do, confirmed by measurement

Three bypass sites (ticket-digest, overlap-judge, code-novelty) must select explicit model classes (trivial, standard, standard respectively) with documented reasoning; one site (review_ticket) is a top-level op and may retain cfg.model by design

A regression test must configure model classes distinct from cfg.model and verify no hand-built sub-call inherits cfg.model; a general provenance guard must flag any future RunRequest with raw cfg that lacks a class binding
